title: Token Cost Surface Mapper — journey sketches & grooming
body:
Purpose
- Capture low-fidelity UX patterns and grooming notes for a Token Cost Surface Mapper: an interactive console panel that lets engineers decompose per-request token spend alongside detailed latency breakdowns.
- Focus intent: give engineers fast, actionable signals to reduce unit cost without regressing latency SLOs or quality.

High-level idea / user journeys
1) Investigate a single slow/high-cost request
   - Open Request Inspector -> Token Cost Surface tab
   - See summary line: total tokens / token-cost ($) / end-to-end latency
   - Timeline scrubber with per-stage markers: front-end serialization, routing, model execution, KV cache lookup, post-processing, network. Hover reveals p50/p95 for stage.
   - Token heatmap shows where tokens occur relative to attention window and whether they triggered KV cache reuse.
   - Action buttons: sample-replay (re-run with debug sampling), quick-quantize-simulate (estimate cost delta with quantized variant), pin-to-watchlist.

2) Bulk analysis for a route/model combo
   - Top-level view for last 24h/7d/30d: per-token unit cost trend, per-request latency distribution heatmap, tail-cost contributors.
   - Filter by client, route, model_version, origin-region, and by whether KV cache hit or miss.
   - Suggested optimization hints (autogenerated): e.g., enable prefix caching for this route; reduce max_tokens by X for <10% quality loss; try model-x-q4b. Each hint links to a simulation panel.

Wireframe notes (low fi)
- Primary nav: Request list -> Inspector -> Token Cost Surface (tabbed).
- Left column: metadata (client, route, model, run_id, tags, user annotations).
- Center: timeline with stacked latency bars per stage; below that a token-level strip showing token counts and density (sparkline overlay).
- Right column: cost breakdown table (tokens-by-type: prompt, completion, assistant-system, embedding ops), delta simulator control, quick actions.
- Inline tooltips must show calculus: example: “Prompt tokens: 124 -> $0.012 at 1.2¢/1k tokens”. Expose unit-rate and period used.

Unique interactions to prototype
- Scrub-to-time: dragging the timeline will update the token strip and show how tokens map to internal KV cache hits (colored badges).
- Cross-filter brushing: highlight any set of tokens and show which sub-component (e.g., tokenizer vs truncation) originated them.
- Cost-simulate slider: slider for effective tokens-per-request multiplier, quantization toggle, batch-size toggle (shows cost per-request vs per-token for different batching scenarios).
- Replay-with-overrides: allow QA to re-run the request server-side with controlled batch size/quantization and get estimated latency/cost from a lightweight dry-run.

Backlog & grooming items (priority order)
- P0: Instrumentation contract (ENG-2412) — add per-token attribution metadata in tracing span (token index -> stage mapping). (owner: infra)
- P0: Backend API: /inspector/requests/{id}/token_surface returning token-level events + cost rates + cache flags. (API spec draft attached to JIRA)
- P1: Timeline control component (fe/ux) with stage stacking and scrub events. (owner: frontend)
- P1: Cost simulator microservice (proto) — compute cost deltas for quantization/ batching/variant selection. (owner: applied-ml)
- P2: Hint engine (heuristics) generating suggested actions and confidence scores. (owner: product)
- P2: Persistence: allow pin/watchlist and annotation comments on a request. (owner: product-console)
- P3: Bulk mode view with aggregation and anomaly detection (future).

Acceptance criteria (for initial MVP)
- Token level view loads for any request id with <= 2s additional load time vs existing inspector baseline.
- Token/event attribution must be complete for 95% of instrumented traffic in staging (missing markers should be surfaced as 'unknown').
- Cost-simulate UI returns a delta estimate with +/-15% accuracy vs benched runs for common quantization variants.
- A user can create a watchlist entry from a token-surface view and receive email/console alerts on recurrence.

Edge cases and open questions
- Requests longer than N tokens (e.g., 64k) — how to present? options: chunked visualization, sampling, or summary-first with expand-to-sample. Prefer summary-first.
- Privacy: token-level content must not be visible for PII-requested traces. Need a sanitizer pipeline and redaction mode. (connect with security & compliance team).
- Billing alignment: token unit rates change over time; historical requests should show the rate that applied at the time of the request and a projected rate for current pricing. Backend needs to return both.
- Non-token costs (e.g., I/O, storage) — include as separate lines in cost table but hide by default.

Telemetry & instrumenting guidance
- New fields in traces: token_index, token_type (prompt/response/system), kv_cache_hit boolean, stage_name, stage_duration_ms, model_variant.
- Expose rollup metrics: tokens_per_request_p50/95, cost_per_request_p50/95, cache_hit_rate_by_route, tail_latency_by_model_variant.
- Provide logs for simulation runs to validate accuracy during rollout.

Prototype tasks for next sprint (note: tactical, not exhaustive)
- Design: One-page wireframes for request inspector tab + modal for simulation (Claire).
- Frontend: implement skeleton panel with timeline component and placeholder data (Samir).
- Backend: minimal token_surface API that returns synthetic tokens for local testing (Diego).
- Applied ML: lightweight cost-simulate model approximator (Samir + Diego).

Mockup ideas (visual cues to include in hi-fi)
- Token heatmap: low->high intensity color ramp; clicking a band filters the timeline.
- Stage microbars: thin stacked bars inside timeline representing sub-milestones (e.g., compile, kernel, allocate).
- Cost attribution waterfall: waterfall chart that shows token->stage->model variant contributions to final cost.
- Inline 'what-if' badges: small badges next to stages that, when clicked, open a pre-filled simulation with recommended setting.

Draft copy for tooltips and microcopy
- Header: "Token Cost Surface" subtitle: "Break down tokens and latency to find high-leverage optimizations"
- Tooltip for cache-hit: "KV cache hit: request avoided 420 token equivalents (est.)"
- Simulator CTA: "Estimate cost change for model-variant or quantization — non-destructive"
- Empty state: "No token attribution available for this request. Try enabling 'detailed tracing' on this route or run a local replay."

Next steps / Decisions needed
- Agree on minimal telemetry schema with infra by 2026-03-20 (owner: Asha).
- Prioritize P0 engineering tickets into sprint next two cycles.
- Legal/security alignment for redaction flow and storage retention.

Notes / loose thoughts (brainstorm fragments)
- Could show per-token semantic labels (instruction / user / system) if tokenizer can tag them — helpful for trimming prompt bloat.
- Consider a "cost spotlight" email that surfaces weekly top-10 regressed routes with one-click suggested fixes.
- Long-term: integrate with Optimize product: closed-loop experiments applying suggested setting changes and measuring real delta.

References and related work
- Existing "Request Inspector" MVP (see PROTO-req-inspector-1) — reuse metadata card and routing.
- Bench notes: microcost-latency-explorer-workshop-notes.json (historic).

End of doc.
